title: Medical necessity: general test
text: A treatment is medically necessary when it is appropriate for the diagnosed condition, in line with accepted medical practice, not mainly for convenience, and the least costly option that is equally effective. Whether a specific treatment meets this test is decided by the medical adviser, not by the claims assistant or the claims handler. Synthetic insurer guideline for the demo, not medical advice.

title: Documents that support a medical claim
text: A medical claim is complete when it has an itemised invoice from a registered provider (date, service code or description, amount), the referral or prescription where the policy requires one, and for hospital or emergency care a discharge note or medical report. Missing items are requested from the claimant; medical reports are sent to the medical adviser only. Synthetic insurer guideline.

title: Physiotherapy
text: Physiotherapy is reimbursed per session up to the policy limit (see POL-2.2). After an operation on the knee, hip or spine, sessions in the first 12 weeks need no referral. More sessions than the limit, or sessions without a clear link to an injury or operation, go to the medical adviser for a necessity opinion. Synthetic insurer guideline.

title: Emergency care abroad
text: Emergency care abroad is care that cannot wait until the insured returns home: an accident, a fracture, acute illness or hospital admission. It is covered under the travel cover (see POL-3.1). The insured must notify the emergency line within 48 hours of an admission. Ambulance transport to the nearest suitable hospital is part of emergency care. Repatriation needs the medical adviser's approval. Synthetic insurer guideline.

title: Causality between an incident and a treatment
text: For accident and travel claims, the treatment must follow from the reported incident: the dates must be consistent and the treatment must fit the injury described. A gap of more than 14 days between incident and first treatment, or a treatment that does not fit the reported injury, is referred to the medical adviser. The claims assistant flags the inconsistency; it does not judge the medicine. Synthetic insurer guideline.

title: Mental health claims
text: Treatment by a registered psychologist or psychiatrist is covered on GP referral for a diagnosed condition (see POL-2.4). The claims assistant checks only that a referral and an itemised invoice are present. The diagnosis, the treatment plan and the number of sessions needed are for the medical adviser. Mental health details never leave the insurer's perimeter. Synthetic insurer guideline.

title: Medical aids
text: Hearing aids, mobility aids and similar devices are reimbursed on prescription from the relevant specialist, at the percentage and limits in the policy (see POL-2.5). A rental for a temporary need, such as a wheelchair while a fracture heals, is reimbursed for the prescribed period. Synthetic insurer guideline.

title: Reasonable and customary charges
text: An invoice is checked against the usual charge for the same service in the same region. A charge far above the usual level is not refused by the assistant; it is flagged for the claims handler, who may pay up to the usual level and ask the provider for an explanation. Synthetic insurer guideline.

title: When the claims handler must be involved
text: Every outcome (pay in full, pay in part, reject, ask for documents) is the claims handler's decision. The assistant prepares a recommendation with the policy clauses and criteria it rests on and the questions it could not answer. Suspected fraud, disputed policy wording and exclusions go to the legal reviewer. Synthetic insurer guideline.

title: Lost or damaged luggage
text: A luggage claim needs proof of value (receipts, bank statements or photos), and for loss by an airline the property irregularity report; for theft, a police report within 24 hours. Payment is limited per item and per trip (see POL-3.2). Items above the per-item limit are paid up to the limit. Synthetic insurer guideline.
